novel_features.name: Credit Burn Timeline
novel_features.description: Track credit consumption over time with daily snapshots, showing per-endpoint burn rate trends
novel_features.rationale: Requires SQLite time-series of usage snapshots that no single API call provides
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent needs to understand cost trends before deciding whether to use basic or advanced search depth

novel_features.name: Sitemap Diff
novel_features.description: Compare current sitemap against the last stored map for the same URL, showing added and removed pages
novel_features.rationale: Requires comparing current API response against historically stored map results in SQLite
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when monitoring competitor sites for new pages or structural changes between crawl runs

novel_features.name: Search Result Diff
novel_features.description: Re-run a previous search and show which results are new, dropped, or changed rank position
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining new API results against stored search history by URL to compute rank deltas
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent needs to detect changes in search landscape for a monitored topic

novel_features.name: Research Archive Search
novel_features.description: Full-text search across all stored research reports, returning matching excerpts with dates and queries
novel_features.rationale: Requires FTS5 index across locally stored research reports that no API endpoint provides
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent needs to find prior research on a topic before deciding whether to run a new research query

novel_features.name: Search-then-Extract Pipeline
novel_features.description: Search for a topic and automatically extract full content from the top N result URLs in one operation
novel_features.rationale: Orchestrates two API calls (search + extract) and stores both with linked provenance
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when building RAG context: one command searches and extracts instead of two separate calls

novel_features.name: Stale Content Detector
novel_features.description: Show extracted pages and crawl results older than N days that may need re-extraction
novel_features.rationale: Queries local SQLite tables by fetched_at timestamp with no API call needed
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent needs to decide which cached content to refresh before answering a question

narrative.headline: Every Tavily feature, plus a local research database that compounds across searches, extracts, crawls, and deep research
narrative.value_prop: The official Tavily CLI is a thin API wrapper with no memory. This CLI stores every search result, extracted page, crawl output, and research report in a local SQLite database. Search offline across all your past results, diff sitemaps across crawl runs, track credit burn over time, and pipe search directly into extraction.

quickstart.comment: Run your first search and cache results locally
Re-run and extract full content from the top 3 results
Query cached results with field selection
See credit burn over the past week

quickstart.command: tavily-pp-cli research --input "Compare LangChain vs CrewAI" --model pro --stream

troubleshoots.fix: Set TAVILY_API_KEY or run tavily-pp-cli config set api_key tvly-...
Check rate limits: 100 RPM dev, 1000 RPM prod. Use --time-range to narrow queries.
Run tavily-pp-cli usage to check remaining credits. Upgrade plan at app.tavily.com.
Try broader query terms, remove domain filters, or switch topic from news to general.
Research endpoint is async. Use --stream for progress. Pro model takes up to 15 minutes.

narrative.when_to_use: Use tavily-pp-cli when you need persistent web research across sessions. It excels at iterative search refinement (diff results across runs), building local content databases from crawled sites, and tracking research costs over time. Prefer it over raw API calls when you want offline access to past results or compound workflows like search-then-extract.
